body.statement:
For the six-vertex graph \(K_6\),
\[
 \operatorname{Cl}_d(K_6)=
 \begin{cases}
 \{\omega_{11}\},&1\leq d\leq6,\\
 \theta_{K_6},&7\leq d\leq9,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad\text{and hence}\qquad ID_{K_6}=7.
\]
The graph \(K_6\) belongs to \(\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(6)\), has directed indegree one, and is not auxiliary-cutset identifiable: \(\operatorname{ACcert}(K_6)=0\).  For every \(n\geq6\), the disjoint union of \(K_6\) with \(n-6\) isolated vertices belongs to \(\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\), has identifying degree seven, and therefore \(D_2(n)\geq7\).
body.proof_tex:
The identity \(\omega_{11}-s_{11}=0\) is a degree-one certificate, so \(\omega_{11}\in\operatorname{Cl}_d(K_6)\) for every \(d\geq1\).  For \(d\leq6\), the rank equalities in \(\mathrm{lem:k6\mbox{-}filtered\mbox{-}elimination}\) show that no coordinate outside \(\{\omega_{11}\}\) is available after \(\omega_{11}\) is adjoined.  Thus \(\{\omega_{11}\}\) is a proper fixed point and
\[
 \operatorname{Cl}_d(K_6)=\{\omega_{11}\}\qquad(1\leq d\leq6). \tag{13}
\]

At degree seven, (6) in that lemma adjoins \(x_3=\lambda_{34}\); its denominator is nonzero by (11).  The identity
\[
 \omega_{14}\Delta_{\!*}-s_{14}\Delta_{\!*}+s_{13}N_{\!*}=0 \tag{14}
\]
also has total degree seven, although it is not needed for the order.  With \(x_3\) available, the four identities
\[
\begin{aligned}
 x_1(s_{13}x_3-s_{14})&=s_{23}x_3-s_{24},\\
 x_2(s_{23}x_3-s_{24})&=s_{33}x_3-s_{34},\\
 x_4(s_{34}x_3-s_{44})&=s_{35}x_3-s_{45},\\
 x_5(s_{35}x_3-s_{45})&=s_{36}x_3-s_{46}
\end{aligned} \tag{15}
\]
are instances of the missing-edge equation (1).  They have total degree three, and their denominators are nonzero by (12).  Hence all five structural coefficients enter the degree-seven closure.  Formula (10) then gives a degree-three certificate for each allowed disturbance coordinate.  Therefore \(\operatorname{Cl}_7(K_6)=\theta_{K_6}\).  Monotonicity in \(d\) gives the same equality for \(d=8,9\).  Combining this with (13) and the already-established closure characterization yields \(ID_{K_6}=7\).

The directed part of \(K_6\) is a chain, so it is acyclic and has indegree one.  Equations (6), (15), and (10), with the nonzero-denominator witness (11)--(12), give a rational inverse on a nonempty Zariski-open subset.  Thus \(K_6\in\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(6)\).  If \(K_6\) were auxiliary-cutset identifiable, the cited auxiliary-cutset degree theorem with \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=1\) would give \(ID_{K_6}\leq1+2+1=4\), contradicting \(ID_{K_6}=7\).  Therefore \(\operatorname{ACcert}(K_6)=0\).

Now add \(n-6\) isolated vertices.  Their disturbance variances equal their observed diagonal variances and have degree-one certificates; all cross-block observed covariances are zero.  Appending these identities to the order (6), (15), (10) proves an upper bound of seven for the padded graph.  Conversely, suppose the padded graph had an identifying order of degree at most six.  Its finitely many denominators are nonzero polynomials in the original model coordinates and the isolated variances.  Choose positive rational values of the isolated variances outside the finite union of their proper specialization zero sets, set every cross-block covariance to zero, and delete the isolated coordinates from the order.  Every remaining identity is then a degree-at-most-six certificate for \(K_6\) with a nonzero denominator.  This contradicts (13).  Positive definiteness is preserved because the padded covariance and disturbance matrices are block diagonal with positive isolated blocks.  Hence the padded graph has identifying degree seven, lies in \(\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\), and proves \(D_2(n)\geq7\).
body.justification: The exact closure calculation calibrates the first two-cycle example and supplies a dimension-feasible lower witness on the full class.
body.gap: Existing missing-cycle arguments supplied only an upper formula degree and did not rule out lower recursive orders using disturbance coordinates.
body.consumer: The full-class elbow now starts from the certified constant lower bound seven rather than from the inadmissible windmill family.
